subject: Follow-up: Hyperscaler comparison & latency A/B test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@nova.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Hyperscaler comparison & latency A/B test plan

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on Nova's production constraints and what success looks like. Quick recap so we have alignment and a proposed next-step plan: 

What I heard from Nova:
- Primary objective: validate inference economics and tail latency under realistic traffic (customer-facing chat workload).
- Key metrics: p95/p99 latency, sustained tokens/sec, and end-to-end cold-start behavior.
- Target latency for initial rollout: p95 below ~150ms on typical 512-token prompts (we noted current hyperscaler baseline ~240–300ms).

What Redwood will do (proposed):
1) Run a controlled A/B benchmark comparing: Redwood hosted endpoint (our managed runtime) vs Hyperscaler-Managed endpoint (your current provider) — using the same model family and model size you supplied.
2) Test matrix (attached): sequence lengths {128, 512, 2048}, concurrency {1, 8, 32}, batch profiles (small/medium/large), and model execution modes (fp16, int8/quant).
3) Measurements to capture: p50 / p95 / p99 / p999 latency, tokens/sec sustained over 30 minutes, cold-start latency, and resource utilization. We'll also capture cost-per-token estimate for each config.
4) Include toggles for prefix/KV cache on/off and continuous batching to show tradeoffs.

Attachments: I attached our proposed test matrix (redwood-test-matrix.xlsx) so you can confirm payload shapes and sampling distribution. Can you also share the sample payloads and any rate-limiting configs we should respect?

Next steps / timeline:
- If you approve the matrix, we can start Redwood-side runs on Wed, Mar 3.
- Deliver a short results deck + raw CSV by Fri, Mar 5 and sync on a 30-min readout the same day.

Would you like us to run the tests against your existing hyperscaler endpoint (we'll need a read-only key / temporary endpoint) or should we run only Redwood vs a simulated baseline using the numbers you provided on call? Either works — we recommend end-to-end runs against the actual endpoint to avoid instrumentation differences.

Thanks — I looped in Vivek (runtime lead) and Laura (solutions engineer) to own the bench and runbook.

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@nova.ai>

Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hyperscaler comparison & latency A/B test plan

Hey Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. We're happy for you to run tests directly against our current hyperscaler endpoint — that will give us the most actionable comparison. I've attached the baseline PDF we pulled yesterday and a small set of sample payloads. Key notes: 

- Baseline (our hyperscaler-managed endpoint) observed over a 1-hour run with mixed sequence lengths: p95 = 270ms (512 tokens, concurrency 8), p99 = 540ms. Sustained tokens/sec ~= 1,150. Cold-starts can spike > 1.5s when the model instance scales up.
- Our model variant: Third-party LLM, 70B, fp16 (we also have an int8 quant build we can share).
- Rate limits: please keep test concurrency capped at 40 parallel requests to match our infra guardrails.

Attachments: nova-bench-results.pdf, sample-payloads.json

I'll provision a scoped API key for a short window if you need to run against the live endpoint. We prefer you not exceed 30 minutes of sustained max concurrency without letting us know first.

—Sam
Sam Ortiz
Head of ML Ops | NovaAI
sam.ortiz@nova.ai | +1 617-555-0227
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@nova.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hyperscaler comparison & latency A/B test plan

Hi Sam / Marissa —

Thanks for the baseline numbers, Sam. Quick note on how we'll run the bench and what we'll report so expectations are explicit: 

Planned test procedure (summary):
- Warmup: 5 minutes at target concurrency to populate KV cache and remove cold start noise.
- Sustained run: 30 minutes at each concurrency level in the matrix, sampling every 5s for latency and throughput.
- Cold-start test: 20 iterations with empty worker pool to capture first-request latency.
- Repeat each test variant twice and report median of runs (we'll include both raw CSVs).

Configuration details we'll vary:
- Batching: continuous batching ON vs OFF and explicit max-batch sizes (2 / 8 / 32).
- KV cache: enabled vs disabled (for chat workloads we expect KV cache to help p95 significantly).
- Quant modes: fp16 (baseline) vs int8-requant (we'll report any quality/latency tradeoffs).
- Sequence lengths: exact payloads from your sample-payloads.json (we'll run the three buckets you indicated).

Success gates (what we'll highlight in the report):
- p95 improvement vs hyperscaler baseline (absolute ms and %).
- p99 behavior and any observed long tails.
- Sustained tokens/sec and cost-per-1M tokens estimate using our pricing model.
- Operational notes: warmup behavior and variance under sustained load.

Can you confirm: a) the live endpoint URL and b) whether the int8 build is stable for production (we can include it as an experimental arm if yes)? If you'd rather not provide a key, we can run the Redwood vs simulated harness using your CSV baseline — just less precise.

I attached a short runbook that our bench engineers will follow (runbook-benchmark.md). We'll start the live runs tomorrow (Thu, Mar 4) morning PT and expect to have a draft report by Fri afternoon. If anything changes on your side (rate limits, maintenance windows), please let us know.

Cheers,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hyperscaler comparison & latency A/B test plan

Vivek / Marissa —

All good to proceed. I've asked infra to spin up a short-lived, scoped API key (read-only for inference) — they'll post the key and endpoint to the secure Drive link below; please pull it and confirm once you have access. Int8 build is experimental but stable enough for a comparative arm.

Secure drive link (will contain key & endpoint): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link

We'll keep an on-call engineer available during your runs in case you trigger any rate guards. Thanks for handling the detailed test plan — looking forward to the results.

—Sam
